# The storyboard

The third stop: the script of the whole page, which the person says yes to. Write it to `docs/story/storyboard.md`.

A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. So this one has a place for each, and an empty place shows.

## The chapters

A row to a chapter:

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The beats

Under each chapter, a row to a beat. A beat is one settled state of the scene and one block of text.

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Screens:** how much scroll the beat takes. One, or more where the scroll works something.
- **How the pieces stand:** a stack, a fan, a ring, a row, a wall, or what the chapter needs. The same pieces in every beat.
- **What is on their faces:** the person's real pictures and words. Name the picture.
- **What the chapter adds:** anything in the scene besides the pieces. Often nothing.
- **Its caption:** a title and a sentence or two, written from the fact sheet.

A caption says nothing the fact sheet does not say. What a project taught the person, what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used: those are theirs to tell you. Where you want such a sentence and do not have it, write the question in its place.

## Someone with thirty seconds

Say how a visitor who does not scroll gets the name, what the person does, one proof of it, and how to reach them. The first screen carries the first three. A rail jumps to any chapter, and one link skips to the close.

## Without the scene

Say what a visitor gets in each case. The text is ordinary HTML over the scene, so all of it is there in every row. Say what stands in for the pieces.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | |
| With reduced motion | |
| With no WebGL | |
| With no JavaScript | |

## The look and the type

Both come from the object's material: plates are ceramic on linen, a status page is dark glass, a paper is white with dark ink. Name two or three looks, each as its ground, its ink, one accent, and the surface of the pieces. The person picks by scrolling, once it is built.

Two typefaces: one for the text, and one for what is printed on the pieces, which belongs to the form.

## Everything else the site needs

Mark every row build, later or never, and say who decided.

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | | |
| A page for each project | | |
| Every project listed | | |
| How to reach them, and a CV | | |
| What others say | | |
| Languages | | |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | | |
| The page for an address that is not there | | |
| A blog | | |
| A chat | | |
| A legal notice, where their country asks for one | | |

## What you ask for

A yes to the script, or what to change. Give the list of what you decided for them with it.

# Storyboard — Aoife Brennan — "The Handover"

Concept A, chosen. Question: *why does the safe way have to be the slow way?*

The object: five cards, the shape and proportion of her real handover sheet, rounded corners, a thin visible edge. Through the whole page they are the same five cards — only their arrangement and their faces change.

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Identify | Opening + Who | Her name, her titles, the question | Cards settle from scattered into one stack | Nothing yet — this chapter only settles |
| 2 | Situation | Where from | The four real stops, dated | Stack unfolds into a row along a timeline | Nothing yet |
| 3 | Background | How | The four things she works from daily | Row closes into a loose ring, turning slowly | Click a card to flip it, for one line on how she actually uses it |
| 4 | Assessment | What + What came of it | The handover sheet, the scanning study, the dashboards, the precepting | Ring opens into a fan; cards come forward one at a time, faces changing as the chapter is scrolled | Toggle old/new sheet; click a workaround to read it in full; click the dashboard card for one more line |
| 5 | Recommendation | Close | The answer, what she's looking for, how to reach her | Fan gathers back into the original stack, the once-blank fifth card turns face-up | Copy email, download CV, open LinkedIn |

No "what others say" chapter: nothing in the material holds it.

## The beats

### 1. Identify

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 Loose | 1 (scroll-tied) | Five cards, scattered loosely above the fold, backs only showing | Blank backs | Nothing | None — wordless |
| 1.1 Named | 1 | A tidy stack, dead centre, resting flat | Top card: "Aoife Brennan" — "CNM1 · Nursing Informatics Link Nurse, one day a week · Cardiac Step-Down, St Brendan's University Hospital, Dublin" | A small tag on the stack's corner: "71% → 94% · 9 months"; the question types in beneath the stack, letter by letter | "Why does the safe way have to be the slow way?" |

### 2. Situation

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 The years | 2 (scroll-scrubbed) | A row: four cards left to right along a line, the fifth held back, closed, off to the right | Card 1: "BSc General Nursing, Liffey University, 2011–2015." Card 2: "Staff Nurse, Coronary Care Unit, St Brendan's University Hospital, 2015–2019." Card 3: "CNM1, Cardiac Step-Down (28 beds), St Brendan's University Hospital, 2019–present." Card 4: "MSc Health Informatics (part-time), Liffey University, 2024–2026." | A thin baseline connecting the four cards | "Eleven years a nurse, six of them in charge of a shift." |

### 3. Background

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 What she works from | 2 | A loose ring: the four daily-tool cards, turning slowly; the fifth stays closed, set outside the ring | Card A: "ISBAR — identify, situation, background, assessment, recommendation." Card B: "The early warning score chart." Card C: "The care plan." Card D: "The audit cycle — plan, do, study, act." | Nothing but the ring's idle turn | "What she works from, every shift." |

Click any one of the four to flip it. Its back holds one line:
- ISBAR → "The form she led a redesign of. Now used on six wards."
- Early warning score → *[no further line held by the material — flip shows the front line only]*
- Care plan → *[no further line held by the material — flip shows the front line only]*
- Audit cycle → "Plan, do, study, act — the shape of the scanning study below."

### 4. Assessment

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 The sheet, before and after | 2 | Ring opens into a fan; the ISBAR card moves to the front | The old handover sheet, then the new one, both blank of patient data | A before/after toggle | "She led a group of five in redesigning the ward's handover sheet. It is now used on six wards." |
| 4.2 Forty hours | 3 (numbers advance on scroll) | Fan continues; a second card comes forward | In sequence: "29% of doses were given without a scan" → "40 hours observed, 22 nurses interviewed" → the three workarounds named one at a time: wristbands that would not scan after a shower; scanners kept on a trolley away from the medication room; scanning from a printed sheet kept in a pocket | Nothing but the sequence itself, scroll-tied | "None of it was laziness. Each workaround saved a nurse one to four minutes a round." |
| 4.3 71 to 94 | 2 (a number climbs on scroll) | Fan continues; same card now shows the fix | "Scanners fixed beside the medication room door. Wristband stock changed. The printed sheets stopped." Beneath it, a single number counting from 71 to 94 | A standing line beneath the number, present throughout the beat: "A ward result: pharmacy, IT, the night staff and me." | "Scanning rose from 71% to 94% in nine months." |
| 4.4 The rest of it | 1 | Fan completes with the remaining two cards | Card: "Preceptor to fourteen newly qualified nurses." Card: "Dashboards built for the falls and pressure ulcer audits." | Nothing | As stated — no outcome is claimed for the dashboards, because the material holds none. |

Click the dashboard card for one more line: "Built in Power BI, from the ward's own audit data." Precepting has nothing further to click.

### 5. Recommendation

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 What moved | 1 | Fan gathers back toward a stack | Top card: "It doesn't — once you move the friction, and not the nurse." | Nothing | The answer to the opening question, stated directly. |
| 5.2 What's next | 1 | Stack, whole again, five cards; the once-blank fifth card turns face-up | Fifth card: "Clinical informatics work, full-time, from 2026." | Nothing | States her aim directly. |
| 5.3 How to reach her | 1 | Stack, at rest, in the exact place it opened in | Email, CV link, LinkedIn | The controls themselves: copy email, download CV, open LinkedIn | "Get in touch." |

## Someone with thirty seconds

The first screen (1.1, Named) carries all three: her name, what she does (the titles), and one proof of it (the small "71% → 94% · 9 months" tag on the stack's corner).

A rail of five tabs — I · S · B · A · R — sits fixed to one side (top on a phone) and jumps straight to any chapter. The R tab is also the one link that skips straight to the close: on hover or long-press it reads "Recommendation — get in touch."

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | Everything above, rearranged: the ring, fan and row become a simple vertical list of cards with light 2D slide/fade between them, no true depth. The I·S·B·A·R rail becomes a slim sticky tab bar pinned to the top. Tap replaces click and hover — tap a card to flip it, swipe for the before/after sheet toggle. The climbing numbers still animate; they are cheap in 2D. |
| With reduced motion | No card drifts, spins, or turns, and no number counts up. Each beat appears already in its finished state the moment it is scrolled into view — the stack is already a stack, the number is already at 94. The flip in Background and the before/after toggle in Assessment happen as an instant swap, not a turn. Everything a scrolling visitor reads, a reduced-motion visitor reads too; only the travel between states is gone. |
| With no WebGL | The cards are drawn flat, in ordinary HTML and CSS, not in 3D. Same words, same order, top to bottom. The ring becomes a small grid, the fan becomes a stacked list, the row stays a row. Nothing is lost but the depth and the turning. |
| With no JavaScript | One static, linear HTML page, in the order Identify, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. No scroll-tied animation, no flip, no toggle. What a flip or a toggle would have shown is printed as plain visible text under the main line instead — the ISBAR card's back-line and the three workarounds are simply there, already on the page. The rail is a plain list of anchor links at the top. Contact is a plain `mailto:` link and a direct link to the CV file. |

## The look and the type

Two looks, each read from the object's own material — a printed ward form:

**Ward paper.** Ground: a warm, pale off-white, like paper. Ink: near-black charcoal. One accent: a muted clinical teal-green. The cards' surface: matte, with a faint printed header rule, a soft short shadow beneath the stack. Calm, daytime, legible.

**Night chart.** Ground: a deep navy-charcoal, like a ward dimmed for the night. Ink: a warm pale cream. One accent: a warm amber-gold, the colour of a call light. The cards' surface: softly lit from within, as if under a nurses'-station lamp, with a thin glowing edge.

My lean is Ward Paper as the default — it reads as a working document, not a mood board — with Night Chart as an easy second if she wants the site to open the way the ward feels at 3 a.m. Either way, the real choice happens by scrolling a built version; nothing here commits her yet.

Type: one humanist sans, plain and warm, for every word the site says to the visitor — headings, captions, body. One typewriter-leaning face, the kind of thing that looks typed onto a form, for anything printed on the cards themselves — the sheet, the tool names, the figures. The two should never be mistaken for each other: one is the site talking, the other is the document itself. Exact families are a build decision, not a planning one.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — the I·S·B·A·R rail, doubling as navigation and as the form's own letters | Me |
| A page for each project | Later — she has one full case study (the scanning study) and three smaller ones; a dedicated page each is more than four items need right now | Me, to confirm |
| Every project listed | Never, for now — nothing beyond the four in Assessment exists in the material | Me, to confirm if more exists |
| How to reach them, and a CV | Build — she is hiring-visible from 2026 and named this as the site's purpose | Her |
| What others say | Never, for now — no quote or reference anywhere in the material | Her (gap, flagged in facts.md) |
| Languages | Never, for now — English only; nothing in the material asks for Irish | Me, to confirm |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build — a link preview carrying her name, title and the question; an icon drawn from the card/tab shape | Me |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — small, in voice: a single card, face down, with the line "no sheet filed under that name" | Me |
| A blog | Never, for now — nothing in the material suggests regular writing | Me, to confirm |
| A chat | Never — nothing in the material asks for it, and a hiring-facing site doesn't need one | Me |
| A legal notice, where their country asks for one | Build — Ireland and the EU require this once a contact form or analytics collects anything | Me (not optional where it applies) |

## What I decided without being asked

Already recorded in `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: no outcome claimed for the dashboards, nothing invented for the Coronary Care years, no photo used anywhere, "what she learned from" left off the site, and the "what others say" chapter dropped for lack of material. Nothing in this storyboard adds to that list.

## What I'm asking you

A yes to this script, or what to change in it.
